summary: platform_optimize: capped-CRF H.264/AAC re-encode with a bitrate ceiling planned per input from display size and frame rate. Deployed 2026-09-25; four real sources run end to end through the production API/queue/worker/download gate; outputs independently verified (fresh decode, ffprobe, VMAF/SSIM against the uploaded source). Raw data: experiments.jsonl (59 encode experiments), production-runs.jsonl (real jobs), quality-analysis.jsonl (independent measurements).

tiktok.published: bitrate >= 516 kbps; file <= 500 MB; up to 10 min; .mp4 .mov .mpeg .3gp .avi; 9:16 >= 540x960 recommended
tiktok.notPublished: no maximum bitrate, no codec, no frame-rate requirement
tiktok.note: Third-party blogs quote '>= 2,000 kbps for 1080p' and '6,000-8,500 kbps' — not TikTok publications; not used as facts.

instagram.publishedReels: MOV/MP4, no edit lists, moov atom at the front; HEVC or H264, progressive, closed GOP, 4:2:0; AAC <= 48 kHz, 1-2 channels, 128 kbps; 23-60 FPS; max 1920 horizontal pixels; VBR 25 Mbps maximum; 300 MB max; 15 min max
instagram.publishedStoriesVideo: same codec/container/bitrate; 100 MB max; 60 s max
instagram.note: A search snippet claiming an '8 MB' Reels size limit was wrong (contradicted by the primary page) and was discarded.

whatsapp.published: MP4/3GP video 16 MB max; only H.264 video and AAC audio; single audio stream or none; H.264 High profile with B-frames is not supported by Android WhatsApp clients — recommends Main profile without B-frames or Baseline; use -movflags faststart
whatsapp.note: The 16 MB limit is a byte limit, so whether a file fits depends on duration as well as bitrate.

youtubeReference.use: The only official per-resolution/frame-rate recommended-bitrate table found from a major platform; used as the ceiling anchor, not as a claim about TikTok/Instagram/WhatsApp internals.

researchedPublishedNumbers.honestUncertainty: No platform publishes a bitrate at which it will skip re-encoding, and TikTok/Instagram/WhatsApp publish only minimums or maximums, never a recommended target. The ceilings are therefore engineering choices anchored on the one official recommendation table, bounded by the published minimum/maximum/limits above, and validated by measurement. Nothing here is a claim about what any platform does internally.

qualityThresholdsCited.justNoticeableDifference: about 6 VMAF points = 1 JND (Netflix, via Ozer 2017; Streaming Learning Center, fetched)
qualityThresholdsCited.vmaf93: 'either indistinguishable from original or with noticeable but not annoying distortion' (Rassool, IEEE 2017, as quoted by https://www.forasoft.com/learn/video-quality/articles-vqm/setting-a-quality-target, fetched)
qualityThresholdsCited.vmaf95: 'on average subjectively indistinguishable from the original video signal' (Kah et al., SPIE 11842-38, 2021, same source); the Joyn study found differences invisible within 2 VMAF points and visible from 3
qualityThresholdsCited.workingRule: top-rung target 93-95 VMAF for premium content on a big screen (same source)
qualityThresholdsCited.caveat: VMAF is relative to the reference and says nothing about the source's own quality; the Netflix VMAF FAQ (github.com/Netflix/vmaf) names the 1080p model vmaf_v0.6.1 (used here) but does not itself define score bands. Only the JND figure and the 93/95 statements above are cited.

sources.description: Real 4K drone clip owned by the site owner (a repeated test asset in this project), 3840x2160 @ 29.97 fps HEVC, rotation=90 (portrait), ~91 Mbps, no audio. NOT 4K60.

Natural 1080p30: first 10 s of Xiph.org Derf test sequence dinner_1080p30.y4m (https://media.xiph.org/video/derf/y4m/), encoded to a camera-like H.264 High CRF 12 (~25 Mbps) + synthetic pink-noise AAC audio (the y4m has no audio).

Real 1080p60: 10 s stream-copied segment (t=245 s) of Big Buck Bunny bbb_sunflower_1080p_60fps_normal.mp4 (Blender Foundation, CC-BY 3.0, https://download.blender.org/demo/movies/BBB/). Animation, and already only ~4.2 Mbps H.264 + MP3 — an already-compressed upload.

Hard natural content: first 8 s of Xiph.org Derf crowd_run_1080p50.y4m (a standard worst-case sequence), 1080p50 (no 60 fps natural source was available), camera-like H.264 CRF 12 (~83 Mbps) + synthetic audio.

rateControl.choice: capped CRF 23 (-maxrate = planned ceiling, -bufsize = 1 s, vbv-init 0.5), not two-pass
rateControl.why: Two-pass hits the target but inflates easy content up to it (a 4.2 Mbps source became 12 Mbps, ~3x its own size) and costs ~55% more time. Capped CRF never inflates and is faster; its only weakness — overshooting the ceiling on short hard clips because the VBV buffer starts full — is removed by a 1 s buffer with vbv-init 0.5 (drone 7998 kbps and crowd 12000 kbps against 8000/12000 ceilings, vs 9231/13204 with the default 2 s buffer).

profile.why: Costs 0.9-2.7 VMAF points (well under 1 JND = 6) or 7-12% bitrate, in exchange for not being rejected by Android WhatsApp clients per Meta's own documentation.

presets.choice: faster by default, veryfast for heavy workloads; superfast/ultrafast excluded
presets.why: faster matches medium quality at ~1.8x speed. superfast produced +62% size on typical content and quality collapses under a cap on hard content.

productionEvidenceTable.ceilingNote: planned at 90% of the 4190 kbps source instead of the 12000 kbps tier ceiling, so a small source is not inflated

honestReading.clearsThreshold: Only 1 of 4 sources clears VMAF 93 at its ceiling. That is what a bitrate ceiling means for content this hard, not a defect: measured CRF sweeps show the bitrate needed for VMAF 93 is ~3.4 Mbps for typical natural 1080p30 but ~20 Mbps for the 4K drone clip at 1080p and ~24 Mbps for crowd_run (linear interpolation of the measured CRF sweep) — several times any platform's published or recommended bitrate — and the 4.2 Mbps BBB source cannot be re-encoded into a smaller file at >= 93 because it is already compressed (plain CRF 23 gave 92.15 at 4.9 Mbps, larger than the source).
honestReading.whatUserGets: Predictable, platform-safe files (H.264 Main/no-B-frames/closed GOP/AAC/moov-first/no edit list) that are 39-91% smaller, with the quality loss controlled by us instead of by a platform's opaque re-encode. Users who only need a container swap for an already-suitable file should still choose remux.
honestReading.measurementNote: An early scoring pass paired frames by timestamp and reported a false VMAF drop (crowd 27, bbb 75) because the no-edit-list output is shifted ~21 ms (one AAC priming block) at every frame after the first; frame counts were identical. Scoring by frame index (with a frame-count guard) gives the figures above; the tool now does this by default.

compat_encode_rotation_bug.before: real job on the 4K portrait clip failed after 698 s with 'output dimensions grew beyond the source'
compat_encode_rotation_bug.after: same clip succeeded in 180 s, dimensionsPreserved=true (production-runs.jsonl)
compat_encode_rotation_bug.note: compat_encode output is 61,524,432 bytes — larger than the 58,592,373-byte source.

environment.measurementFfmpeg: static ffmpeg 7.1 with libvmaf, model vmaf_v0.6.1
environment.experimentHostNote: Shared VPS with load average 17-39 during experiments; speed figures are therefore conservative and noisy, sizes and VMAF are deterministic.
